title: A Letter in a Salt Isles Tin
author: Keddo ko-Oskel, pilot
body:
# Mother

*Written at the lead-house door, the night of the sailing.*

---

The master will sail on the tide. Father has told him the skerries are running and he says the Salt Isles do not wait on Oskel weather, and Father says then the Salt Isles can pilot themselves, and then goes and gets his coat.

So we are going. I am writing this to leave in the tin in case, which Father says is bad luck, so do not tell him.

The fire is lit at the Watch. I can see it from here, as plain as the lamp in our window, and I know it is Bressa on the watch tonight because she keeps it too high, she always does, it throws sparks. So you are not to blame her whatever the master does. The fire is lit. I can see it.

We will be home for the thaw. Keep my boots dry.

*Keddo*

title: The Unroped's Roll
author: kept at Ghastow, in several hands
body:
# Those who came up the moor

*Name, clan that was, price asked, and paid or not.*

---

Gorrm, that was Ghast. A hundred head, for a fall. **Not paid.** Struck: paid by us, in advance, at the stones.

Ilsa, that was Brindle. A year's ore, for a cart gone down the Edge. **Not paid.**

Dennek, that was Rudd. A verse, for a man nobody else would miss. Rudd would not sing it. **Not paid.**

The boy, that was Oskel, no name given, he will not say it. Priced at nothing. **Paid.** He says that one was fair.

*At the foot, in Gorrm's hand:* A price paid is a price paid. We will pay them all, in the grooves, where the road can see. Then let the Moot say what we owe.

title: The Last Bier-List
author: Hethra ko-Skarl, memory-keeper
body:
# Carried up

*The last page of a Skarl keeper's bier-list, kept at Orrdun's door.*

---

Ald ko-Skarl, herdsman, eighty winters. Carried up by his sons. Sung in. Niche nine hundred and four.

The child of Tavva, unnamed, one winter. Carried up by her mother alone, who would not be helped. Sung in. Niche nine hundred and five.

Orrin ko-Skarl, drowned at the Spout. Carried up by the clan. Sung in. Niche nine hundred and six.

*Then, in the same hand, smaller:* The Breath did not come for Orrin. I sang him again. It did not come. I have sent the bearers down and told them not to carry any more until I send word. I will sing the one before him. Somebody in this hall must be first in line, and it must be possible to find out who.

*The rest of the page is names, the same names, over and over, in a hand that gets larger and less like writing.*

title: A Spout-Keeper's Slate
author: a Skarl keeper of the Spout, long before Ossa
body:
# What the water said

*Chalked on a slate and left where the lake begins.*

---

Came in on a rope to see where the tokens come from. The rope is not long enough.

The water is not cold here. It is the temperature of a hand.

There is something kneeling at the lake. It has its hands in the water. It lifts them, and something is in them, and it opens them and lets the water have it. It does this as if it had been asked to.

I am going back. If the Skarl ask, the Spout is clear and the water is sweet and there is nothing to see.

title: A Tag of Lead
author: stamped at Ghastow
body:
# Hung on the gate

*Stamped into lead with a nail, one letter at a time.*

---

KHARROW. HERDSMAN'S DEATH. 1003. A HUNDRED HEAD. NOT PAID.

*On the back, scratched with a knife:* It was a fall. It was a fall. It was a fall.

title: A Bearer's Knots
author: a Skarl bier-bearer
body:
# Carried up

*A knot for each bier, read back by feel.*

---

Forty knots. My mother's is the first. My father's is the twelfth.

*A gap, and one knot tied very tight:* The last one. The keeper went in behind it to sing, and sent us down, and said she would send word.

*No more knots. Tied to the end, a bone token of the Skarl, and a note in chalk on the hide:* We are still waiting for word. Every dusk the herd hears her. We have stopped carrying. We have not stopped listening.

title: Chalked at the Knees
author: a Skarl water-keeper
body:
# Do not drink

*Chalked large enough to read by moonlight.*

---

The water in there has not decided yet.

It goes in cold and comes out colder at the Spout two days on, and in between it runs past something that is still drinking.

If you go in, go on a rope, and come out on it.

If you hear it lift its hands out of the lake, you are too near.

title: The Weather on the High Moor
author: Maudry Pennant, of the Circle
body:
# Readings, the Breathing Stones

*Kept twice a day in a Tollmere hand.*

---

Glass rising, hole breathing out, 14 units. Glass falling, hole breathing in, 15 units. As a sponge would. Karst.

Year's sum: in, 91 units more than out.

Year's sum: in, 104 units more than out.

*In the margin, in the same hand but hurried:* A sponge does not take in more than it gives. Not for six years. Not with nothing coming out anywhere else.

*The last line:* Stopped breathing out. Drawing in only. 3rd week. I do not know where it is going and I would like to.

title: Lintels Out of Skerrfall
author: Hodd ko-Brindle, quarry-master
body:
# Sent

*Stone, length, and whose door it went over.*

---

A lintel of nine feet, for the Moot hall at Kharrow. A lintel of six, for the Dreugh ninth door. A lintel of four, a child's grave at Oskelcrag, no charge.

*Thirty years of them, a line each.*

*The last line:* A lintel of eleven feet, already laid, over a door we did not cut, in a stone that is not stone, warm. Not sent. Not cut. Not mine.

title: The Wall-Book at the Briar's End
author: two keepers, turn about
body:
# Walked the wall

*One line a day. Skarl hand, then Woodfolk hand, then Skarl.*

---

Walked it. Sound.

Walked it. Sound. Briar green to the gap.

Walked it. A rib loose at the third bay. Wedged.

Walked it. The third bay is holding. Your wedge is good.

*A long gap in the Skarl hand, then:* Walked it. Pushed out. From our side.

*The Woodfolk hand, under it, the same day, which has never happened before:* I heard it too.

title: Prices, the North Road
author: Graddo ko-Kharrow
body:
# What a life is worth on the North Road

*By the Moot's leave, as reckoned at the Hut.*

---

A herdsman in his prime: forty head, or ten years' work for the family.

A smith: twelve years' work, and the forge fired for the family's use for life.

A memory-keeper: a verse, sung every spring, by the clan that owes it, for as long as the clan is a clan.

A child: whatever the mother says. She has never yet said a number.

An unroped man or woman: nothing. *Somebody has cut under it, deep, with a knife:* WE WILL SEE.

title: The Sweeping Round
author: Bressa, knotted
body:
# Where to sweep

*Heather knots on a string. Read by feel in the dark.*

---

A knot for each seat at the Old Moot. Eight. The clans sweep seven.

A knot for the Skerry Watch. Tied twice, tight.

A knot for the Unroping Post by the Oskelcrag road. That one is not for sweeping. That one is for standing at, once a year, until the rope that is mine has gone to nothing, and it has not gone to nothing yet.

title: The Turned Stone
author: a Skarl herder, in charcoal
body:
# What was on the face

*Rubbed with charcoal on birch bark, as fast as I could.*

---

A closed hand, cut deep. Under it a line of Skerrish, worn nearly off: *...OW. WE KEPT THE ...*

The rest is gone into the stone.

*Scrawled under it:* I did not turn it. It was turned when I came. I am not a verse in debt to the Moot. Somebody else is.

title: A Courier's Letter
author: a Tollmere courier
body:
# To the gate-warden at Windgate

*Sealed with the Tallymen's wax, and never delivered.*

---

The Guild asks the gate-warden what toll he is taking on a pass nobody can cross, and on whose authority, and to whom he is remitting it.

*Under the seal, in pencil, the courier's own:* Caught out by the dark. Rang the shelter bell. Nobody came. The wolves came. I am going to the hole in the ground because the wolves came from there and are all out here now, and it is the only place on this moor they are not.

title: What They Carried
author: a Skarl herder, on the pavement
body:
# Watched from the heather

*A scratch for each bone carried.*

---

Three ribs, the long ones, first. Then knuckles, two at a time, in their arms, like a child carrying apples.

They lay them down very gently. They measure the gap with a hand before they lay the next.

One of them stood at the end of the line all day with nothing in its arms, facing south, toward the ford.

I have not told the Rudd. I do not know how to tell a Rudd that something is counting.

title: Fleece, Skarl Ridge
author: Jory Wool, of the Mere
body:
# Bought

*In a Valish hand, the numbers in Valish and the notes in bad Skerrish.*

---

Forty fleeces, good, off a Skarl woman with a dog like a wolf. Stayed the night. The dog has not decided about me.

Forty fleeces. Stayed the winter.

*Nineteen years of forty fleeces.*

*The last entry, in another hand, Skerrish:* No fleece bought this year. The buyer is under the ridge. His name is on the lintel, cut badly, by him. It stays.

title: Tides at the Oskel Shore
author: the Salt Isles factor
body:
# Tides, and lead

*In Sedgish with a lisp, the numbers in Valish.*

---

High water two hours after the moon. Skerries running on the ebb; stand off until the Watch fire is let down.

Forty pigs of Oskel lead, weighed and stamped.

*The last season:* Master will not wait for the Watch. Master says the Watch is Oskel business. Pilot says the Watch is the sea's business and the sea does not care whose it is. We sail on the flood.

title: Set Out Before Cutting
author: Haska ko-Ghast, stone-cutter
body:
# The stones, and who is under them

*Each name chalked on a slate and copied here before the first cut.*

---

Eleven. Ghast and Kharrow both, the year of the broken bridge, each remembered by the Song after the stones forgot them. Each set out, each cut, each sung.

*The twelfth, in a hand that does not want to write it:* A living man. Paid in advance, the letter says. I have set it out. I will not cut the last three letters. A stone for the dead goes up after, not before, and if nobody else on this moor keeps that rule, I do.

title: The Seven Bricked Doors
author: a Skarl herder, sheltering
body:
# Copied by lamplight

*The chalk on each bricked door, as it is.*

---

The first door: a mark, Kharrow's, and a number, one.

The second: Dreugh's, and two. And so on: Brindle, Ghast, Rudd, Oskel, Skarl, three to seven.

The open door, the eighth: no mark. A number, chalked fresh, a finger's width high: *nought*.

*Under it:* I did not go down. I am telling everybody I did not go down, so that it is true.

title: Fished Out
author: a scree-hag's string, read by a herder
body:
# On the string

*Counted off it, in order, by whoever took it down.*

---

A child's rope-toggle, Brindle-knotted. A Valish penny, no king on it. A bone token cut with a closed hand. A tooth, not human, not wolf. A key to no door in the heights.

*Last on the string, tied on with a hair:* a smooth stone with a name scratched on it, and the name is mine, and I have never been to the Hidden Tarn before today.

title: Balked
author: an Oskel herder
body:
# Would not go through

*A notch a beast. The Oskel sell a beast that balks.*

---

One balked. Two. The whole herd.

The whole second herd.

*On the flat of the stick:* Went through myself to show them. Nothing on the far side. The heather, the moor, the crag-wolves where they always are. Came back through. The herd looked at me as if I had come back from somewhere.

title: On the Inner Face
author: unknown
body:
# Scratched with something sharp

*On the side of the bone that faces the fell, not the Briar.*

---

KEPT FROM BOTH SIDES.

*Under it, fresher, in a different hand:* by whom

*Under that, fresher still, in the first hand again:* by us

title: Where the Grass Is
author: an Oskel spoil-picker, a child
body:
# The grass

*A cross for each tuft. Drawn every day.*

---

One tuft, at the bottom of the spoil, by the old shed.

Two. Three. A line.

*The crosses go up the slate in a line toward a circle marked MINE.*

*At the top:* It's nearly at the mine now. Mam says do not walk along it. I walked along it. It's warm, like the grass is on top of something breathing.

title: On the Parapet
author: copied by a Rudd herder
body:
# Chalked on the parapet

*In a Kharrow hand, the Rudd herder says, from the loops.*

---

FORTY HEAD WENT OVER THIS BRIDGE THAT OWED THE GORGE A TOLL.

*Rubbed half out, and under it, in the same hand, smaller:* and we never said. and we are not saying now. we are standing here so that you know we are not saying it.

title: Kept In
author: the Oskel herders, turn about
body:
# The fire at the dale head

*A line a night: who kept it, and the mine.*

---

Kept in. Mine singing.

Kept in. Mine singing.

*Years of the same line.*

Out. Out, the one night, the peat wet through. Mine silent. We sat and listened to nothing till dawn.

Kept in. Mine singing again, and a new note in it, like somebody trying a word.

title: Counting the Spine
author: a Rudd child, sent up to practise
body:
# One, two

*Counted out loud and written down after.*

---

Twenty-six bones in the heather. Twenty-six!

Counted again: twenty-six.

*Crossed out:* The last three have gone. There are holes where they were, and drag-lines in the heather going away. Two lines go north. One line goes south, to the beck.

I am not supposed to count what is not there. Grandmother says you only sing what you can touch.

title: To the Moot, About the Bones
author: a Skarl herder
body:
# A complaint

*To be read at the spring sitting, if the herder can bring himself to.*

---

The bones in the Bonefield have lain where they lie since before the Skarl. My herd grazes among them. My herd knows where every one is.

This summer they are in rows. Ribs with ribs. Knuckles with knuckles. My herd will not graze among them now; they stand at the edge and look.

I ask the Moot who gave anybody leave to tidy the Bonefield. I would like it put back.

title: The Mark on the Far Anchor
author: a Ghast mason
body:
# The far anchor

*Rubbed at low water, hanging off the near end by a rope.*

---

The near anchor is Ghast's, cut by us. The far anchor has three marks. Kharrow's, as the treaty says.

Under Kharrow's, older: a closed hand.

Under the hand, older still, worn nearly off, a mark I do not know, like a mouth.

*A note to the clan:* The bridge had three builders. We only ever paid two.

title: Pitch on the Chains
author: the Rudd tappers
body:
# Coated

*Every autumn, the four chains in treaty order.*

---

Kharrow's: coated. Dreugh's: coated. Brindle's: coated. Ghast's: coated, and loosened one link by the Moot's word, and coated again at the new link.

*Twenty autumns of the same.*

*This year:* The pitch from the red stand will not go on Ghast's chain. It runs off. It goes on the other three like any pitch. We have used the old pitch on Ghast's. Nobody will tell the Moot. It is only pitch.

title: An Oath
author: unsigned
body:
# Pushed into the rib

*Written small, on birch bark, and folded twice.*

---

I swear on the giant's bones, which do not forget, that I will not tell my brother what I saw on the Edge the night the herdsman fell. I swear that I will carry it. I swear it is not mine to tell.

*Folded inside, a second slip, newer, in the same hand, older:* The one it would have saved is at Ghastow. I am still carrying it. The bones have not let me put it down.

title: The Last Riser
author: whoever climbed it
body:
# At the top of the stair

*Rubbed onto a shirt, because there was nothing else.*

---

The stair stops at a sheer face where the snow has never melted. The last riser is as high as a man's chest, and cut into it, in letters the size of a hand, not Skerrish and not Oroth:

*A line of marks like footprints going up, and then none.*

And under them, in Skerrish, much smaller, much newer, cut by a knife: WE WENT UP. DO NOT FOLLOW. WE WILL SEND WORD.

title: Chalked on the Witness-Slate
author: whoever sat on the bench
body:
# Seen paid

*The slate by the Stones, for the witnesses: who laid it, for whom, and who saw.*

---

Rudd to Skarl: nine head and a summer's grass, for the boy at the Bone Ford. Seen: Orsk, Ymma, a tinker.

Brindle to Kharrow: a year's ore, for the cart off the Edge. Seen: Graddo, two drovers.

Ghast to nobody: coin, old, laid at night. Seen: nobody. *(and under it, in a different chalk)* I saw. I will not say.

title: A Child's Copy-Slate
author: a child, by the hand
body:
# THE HEIGHTS

*Copied off the stone, in Valish, many times, the letters getting better and the S still backwards.*

---

THE HEIGHTS THE HEIGHTS THE HEIGHTS

THE HEIGHTS

*(At the bottom, in the same hand, smaller:)* Da says the Brindle cut the Valish off because the Vale cheated them in the Charter. Mam is from the Vale. I am putting it back so she can read where she lives.

title: The Dale Watch, by the door
author: the Ghast watch
body:
# Up the dale

*Who came up, and which side of the Moot they said they stood on.*

---

A drover, Brindle. The Moot's side.

A tinker. No side. Let up; tinkers are no side.

Two Kharrow on Moot business. The Moot's side, they said, which is what Kharrow always say.

**Midnight.** The horn. Nobody in the house but me, and I was asleep, and I have the horn's frost on nothing but the mouthpiece. Nobody came up the dale. In the morning there were tracks coming down it.

title: Ropes on the Cairn
author: Tam ko-Brindle, herder
body:
# Ropes on the Rope Cairn, this spring

---

The Haddos' two, red. The Eddrick girl, blue, very short, she was quick. My own boy's, undyed, longer than mine was, he was slow and I am glad.

One more. Black hemp, old as the cairn, tied in a hitch with a turn too many. The length of a child of six. No family on the Edge owns it.

I asked old Ushka ko-Kharrow, who knows every verse. She said that hitch was tied before the Rope-Song had seven verses, and then she would not say anything else, and went home early.

title: Under the Paint-Pot
author: the Dreugh eldest
body:
# Midsummer

*For whoever paints Dreugh after me.*

---

Grey-blue, two coats, the second thin. Start at the shoulder and work down; the rain does the rest.

Paint round the eighth socket as well. Everybody does. Nobody says why. My mother said her mother said: so it is ready.

*(Added, this year, in a shakier hand:)* It is not empty any more. I painted round it anyway. I did not paint the stone. I did not want to touch it, and when I put my hand near it, it was warm.

title: A Leave-Token
author: left at Ghastfoot
body:
# Asked leave

*Scratched on both sides of a clay token, the way travellers up Ghast Dale ask the skull.*

---

Haska ko-Ghast asks leave to go up and cut the Red Moor's stones.

*(other side)* The skull that is up there now is clay. Haska made it. The real one is at the Red Moor, under the twelfth stone, where it can see the dead of the bridge. Ghast does not know. Ghast will find out when Haska is under a stone herself.

title: The Kharrow Memory-Verse
author: Ushka ko-Kharrow, memory-keeper
body:
# Said at the cairns, once a year

---

*Kharrow who went up and did not come down,*
*here is your name, said, and said, and said;*
*the mountain keeps your bones, the clan keeps you,*
*and what is kept is never wholly dead.*

---

Forty-one years, and every name in its place. When I am under a slate myself, whoever says them: say them all. Do not leave out the ones you did not like. That is what the mountain does, and we are not the mountain.

title: Bells in the Swallow
author: a Brindle miner
body:
# Dropped, and heard

---

My da's bell, dropped 1001. Heard at the spring the next morning, faint.

My own, dropped 1004. Heard at noon.

The Haddo boy's, 1011. Not heard.

Mine again, 1019. Not heard. Something at the spring, though, three days on: a bell, not mine, older, green. It came out of the spring in the Brindle's own water and nobody in Brindlecrag owns it.

The miners say the beck passes the singing shaft on the way down. I say it passes something that keeps bells.
